Heard Mr. B. Baral, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. P.K. Muduli, learned Addl.
Government Advocate appearing for the State-opposite parties.

3. The petitioner has filed this writ petition challenging the order dated 02.05.2023 passed by the Collector, Cuttack, in pursuance of the order dated 06.12.2022 passed by this Court in W.P.(C) No.
31406 of 2022, which was communicated to the petitioner on 03.05.2023 by the Land Acquisition Officer (Civil), Cuttack under Annexure-1.

By the impugned order, the Collector, Cuttack, while considering the grievance made by the petitioner in his representation dated 28.03.2022, on verification of the records, found that the compensation amount of Rs.3,66,255/- has been paid to the petitioner in respect of land pertaining to plot no.1306 measuring Ac. 0.11 dec. under khata no.292; plot no.1336 measuring Ac.0.14 dec. under khata no. 534/102 and plot no. 1314 measuring Ac. 0.10 dec. under khata no. 534/103 of Mouza-Choudwar towards decreetal dues basing on the order dated 24.07.2008 passed by the learned Civil Judge (SD) 1ST Court, Cuttack vide L.A. Case No.30/2006 arising out of LAMC No. 131/2002 under Section 28(A) of L.A. Act filed by Suresh Chandra Nayak & others Vs. State of Odisha & others.

entities.text: Suresh Chandra Nayak & others Vs. State of Odisha & others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Once the decree of the civil court has already been satisfied, now, at this point of time, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the order dated 02.05.2023 passed by the Collector, Cuttack, which was communicated to the petitioner on 03.05.2023 by the Land Acquisition Officer (Civil), Cuttack under Annexure-1.
4.
At this point of time, learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the petitioner is entitled to get interest for the delayed payment of the compensation amount.
In such view of the matter, it is open to the petitioner to pursue his remedy before the appropriate forum.
